question: Get from the airport to Ulsan
answer: From Incheon: AREX to Seoul Station, then the KTX to Ulsan, or a direct bus (about 5 hours). From Gimhae: a limousine bus, about an hour.
steps: Incheon by train: take the airport railroad (AREX) to Seoul Station, then a KTX to Ulsan Station (울산역, also signed 통도사). Book the KTX in KORAIL+ or on the Korail website.
Incheon by bus: direct buses to Ulsan leave from both terminals several times a day. No change, room for luggage.
Gimhae (Busan): an airport limousine bus reaches Ulsan in about an hour.
Leave 2 to 3 hours after landing for immigration and luggage before your train or bus.
From KTX Ulsan Station to UNIST: a taxi takes 10 to 15 minutes. Show 유니스트 and your dorm name.

question: Take a bus
answer: Find the route in Naver Map, tap your transit card when you get on and again when you get off.
steps: Search your destination in Naver Map or KakaoMap and pick the bus option. The app shows the bus number, the stop and when the next bus comes.
Get on at the front door and tap your T-money card (or a Korean bank card that works as one).
Press the bell (하차벨) before your stop and get off at the back door. Tap your card again on the way out, so a transfer within the time limit is free or cheaper.
Do not count on cash. Ulsan started cashless city buses on some routes in October 2026 and plans to make all routes cashless in early 2027 (card or bank transfer only).

question: Call a taxi
answer: Use K.Ride (no Korean number needed) or Kakao T, or wave one down on the street.
steps: Before you have a Korean number, use K.Ride: English screens, foreign cards, and a translated chat with the driver.
Once you have a Korean number, Kakao T has the most taxis. You can choose to pay the driver directly if your card fails in the app.
On the street, wave at a taxi with a red light showing it is free (빈차).
Show the address in Korean or a map pin, and say 유니스트로 가 주세요 if you are going to campus. Most taxis take cards.

question: Order food delivery
answer: Baemin has English and takes foreign cards. Coupang Eats and Yogiyo usually need a Korean number.
steps: Open Baemin, switch it to English, and set your address exactly as it is written in Korean.
Find out where your dorm wants deliveries left: drivers often cannot enter the building.
Add a request for the rider, such as 문 앞에 놔 주세요 (leave it at the door).
If sign-up or payment fails, try Shuttle, which is built for foreigners.
Once you have a Korean number, Coupang Eats and Yogiyo are worth comparing for deals.

question: Send a parcel
answer: Inside Korea, the cheapest way is a convenience store. Abroad, go to a post office (EMS).
steps: Inside Korea: GS25 and CU convenience stores send parcels, including cheap store-to-store delivery (반값택배). Have the address ready in Korean.
Abroad: go to a post office (우체국) and send it by EMS. A passport is accepted for small international parcels.
Some CU stores also send international express parcels through DHL.
Customs may ask what is inside and its value; food must be sealed and shelf-stable.

question: Buy second-hand things
answer: Karrot is where everyone buys and sells, but it needs a Korean number. Before that, ask in Everytime or your dorm chats.
steps: Before you have a Korean number: ask your buddy, the dorm group chat or the Everytime market board. Students leaving at the end of a semester sell fans, rice cookers and bikes.
With a Korean number (and ARC): sign up for Karrot, set your neighbourhood to the campus area and search in Korean (선풍기 fan, 자전거 bicycle).
Meet in a public place in daylight, check the item before paying, and pay by bank transfer or cash.
Keep all chat inside the app.

question: Find a pharmacy
answer: Search 약국 in Naver Map. At night or on holidays, use E-Gen to see what is open.
steps: Search 약국 (pharmacy) in Naver Map or KakaoMap. Look for the large 약 sign on the street.
At night or on a holiday, check the E-Gen app or website for open pharmacies and clinics. Ulsan has had public late-night pharmacies since 2022; they usually close around 1 a.m.
Late at night, convenience stores sell basic fever and pain medicine.
Describe the problem simply (머리가 아파요, I have a headache) or show a Papago translation.
In an emergency, call 119.

question: Pay without a Korean card
answer: Foreign Visa and Mastercard cards work in most shops. Apps are harder: use the ones that accept foreign cards, and keep some cash.
steps: In shops, cafes, taxis and kiosks, a foreign Visa or Mastercard usually works. If asked 일시불이요?, say 네.
Keep some cash in won for topping up your T-money card and for small stalls.
In apps, foreign cards work in Baemin, Shuttle, K.Ride and CatchTable Global; many other apps reject them.
WOWPASS is a prepaid card for foreigners that you top up with cash at its machines.
Toss lets you sign up with a passport and use a prepaid card before you have an ARC.
Kakao Pay needs a Korean card; some shops let visitors scan its QR code with a foreign wallet through Alipay+.

question: Get a Korean phone number
answer: A prepaid SIM or eSIM with a 010 number works on your passport. Most identity checks in apps need a line registered with your ARC.
steps: Before you fly or at the airport: buy a prepaid SIM or eSIM that includes a Korean 010 number, not a data-only plan. A passport is enough.
Know the limit: lines on a passport often cannot pass identity verification (본인인증), which banks, Coupang and Karrot use.
After you get your ARC: register the line with your ARC or move to a monthly plan. Ask whether you can keep the same number; do not assume it carries over.
Your number is tied to your stay: a line registered to a student can be suspended when the permitted stay ends.

question: Get my Residence Card (ARC)
answer: Register within 90 days of arrival, in person at the immigration office, after booking on HiKorea. Ask UNIST International Affairs first.
steps: Foreigners staying longer than 90 days must apply for a Residence Card (formerly the Alien Registration Card, ARC) within 90 days of entry.
You cannot apply online: book an appointment through HiKorea, then go to the immigration office in person.
Ask UNIST International Affairs which documents and fee to bring, and whether they organise the visit.
The card is not issued on the spot, so apps that need an ARC have to wait a little. Since 2025 there is also a mobile Residence Card in the Mobile ID app, which needs a phone in your own name.
Questions in English: the immigration contact centre, 1345.
